summary: createAiChatHandler reads a view context (what the user had open when sending the newest message) from the body field glirastesViewContext and gives it to the model as a data block. On by default; nothing sends the field yet, so an unchanged app sees no change.
howTo: Nothing to do. The browser side follows in a later release. To prepare: viewContext: false turns it off (null counts as not set); viewContext: { types, maxEntries, facts: { order: z.object({ status: z.string() }) } } narrows the accepted entity types (by default every type the request's tools declare with outputEntities / inputEntities), the entries per message and the facts kept (only for a type with a schema here). history must be 'none' for now; an invalid option throws when the handler is created. The runtime container turns it off until its option chat.viewContext comes. With piiShield the values are shielded like tool results (audit: anonymize-result, counted in totalToolCalls) and checked again. The block has at most 2,966 characters (roughly 850 tokens when full); maxEntries and facts make it smaller. Only the built-in stream handler adds the block; continuations, guardrail-blocked requests, clarification answers, direct commands and a custom streamHandler get none; guardrails and hideIds do not see it. Known limit: a label is cut to 60 characters before the PII shield sees it, so a cut e-mail address, IBAN or phone number at its end may reach the model as a plain-text fragment (ids and facts are never cut); the fix follows before the browser side. Until then a client of your own that sends the field should cut labels to at most 60 characters or set viewContext: false.
